'''George Iwao Fujimoto''' (July 1, 1920 – April 30, 2023) was an American chemist of Japanese descent. 

==Life and career==
Fujimoto was born in [[Seattle, Washington]] on July 1, 1920.<ref>{{cite web|title=United States Public Records Index|url=https://familysearch.org/pal:/MM9.1.1/KTVP-2H6|publisher=FamilySearch|accessdate=15 October 2013}}</ref> During his studies at Harvard his family was imprisoned in an American [[internment camp]] [[Minidoka National Historic Site|Minidoka]] in [[Idaho]]. He discovered the [[Fujimoto–Belleau reaction]], which is named after him and [[Bernard Belleau]]. 

Fujimoto was widowed at the age of 99 when his wife Mary died on December 17, 2019.<ref>[https://www.scarsdalenews.com/obituaries/mary-yano-fujimoto/article_3b430df4-2357-11ea-8ba6-23599b900e19.html May Yano Fujimoto obituary]</ref> He died on April 30, 2023, at the age of 102.<ref>{{cite web |title=George Iwao Fujimoto |url=https://www.forevermissed.com/george-iwao-fujimoto/about |website=Forever Missed |access-date=31 May 2023}}</ref>
